2. Choosing an Embedding Model

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: text-embedding-3-small and text-embedding-3-large are available model choices

blocks.text: OpenAI offers several embedding model options, generally trading off vector quality against cost and vector size, a smaller model is cheaper and faster but may capture slightly less nuance than a larger one, choosing between them depends on your actual accuracy needs and budget.

code.content:
response = client.embeddings.create(
    model="text-embedding-3-small",
    input="The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog.",
)
vector = response.data[0].embedding

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: Input text provided calls the embeddings endpoint, returning a vector array

blocks.text: This connects directly to the request body and response body topics covered in an earlier module, the request specifies a model and the input text, the response returns a numeric vector array representing that text, ready to be used directly for similarity comparison or storage.
4. Batching Multiple Inputs

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A single string input is compared against a batch array of many inputs

blocks.text: The input field accepts either a single string or an array of many strings at once, sending several texts in one batched call is meaningfully more efficient than making a separate call per text, this connects directly to the efficiency principles covered in the earlier Prompt Optimization module.

blocks.text: 5. The dimensions Parameter

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: A full dimension vector can be reduced by the dimensions parameter

blocks.text: Some embedding models let you request a reduced vector size directly through a dimensions parameter, trading a small amount of representational precision for a smaller, cheaper to store and faster to compare vector, useful when storage or comparison speed genuinely matters more than maximum precision.

blocks.title: This is a genuine, practical tradeoff worth understanding
blocks.content: A smaller embedding dimension reduces storage and comparison cost at real scale, the right choice depends on how much that efficiency actually matters for your specific application versus the marginal precision a full dimension vector provides.

7. Cost Considerations

blocks.title: Diagram summary
blocks.content: Many small, separate calls are compared against one larger batched call

blocks.text: This connects directly to token optimization, covered in an earlier module, embeddings are typically priced per token of input text, batching many inputs into fewer calls does not reduce the actual token cost, but it does reduce request overhead and total latency, worth doing at real volume regardless.
8. A Worked Embeddings Example

A document search feature generates embeddings for every chunk of a large document collection in batched calls, storing the resulting vectors in a vector database, then generates an embedding for each incoming user query and compares it against the stored vectors to find the most relevant chunks, exactly the retrieval mechanics covered in the earlier RAG Prompting module.
9. This Topic vs the Later Embeddings APIs Module

This topic covers OpenAI specific embeddings endpoint concretely, the later Embeddings APIs module in this course covers embeddings more generally across different providers and use cases, both worth understanding together for a complete picture.
Worked Example

A team building a document search feature initially generates embeddings one document chunk at a time, making thousands of separate API calls for a large document collection, resulting in significant overhead and slow overall processing time.

Switching to batched calls, sending many chunks together in a single request, dramatically reduces the total processing time for the same document collection, while the actual token cost stays essentially the same, demonstrating the real efficiency gain batching provides even without reducing the underlying cost.
Common Mistakes

items: Generating embeddings one input at a time instead of batching many inputs into fewer calls
Choosing the largest available embedding model regardless of whether the extra precision is actually needed
Not considering the dimensions parameter when storage or comparison speed genuinely matters more than maximum precision
Confusing this specific OpenAI endpoint with the broader, cross-provider embeddings concepts covered in a later module

blocks.text: Practice

Generate embeddings for five short texts using a single batched call, then compare the vectors for two genuinely similar texts against two genuinely different texts, confirming the similar pair produces vectors that are closer to each other.
Key Takeaway

OpenAI embeddings endpoint converts text into a numeric vector representation, choosing between available models based on your accuracy and cost needs, batching many inputs into fewer calls for real efficiency, and optionally reducing vector dimensions for storage or speed, this concrete endpoint is exactly the mechanism behind the RAG retrieval systems covered in an earlier module.
